You are an experienced NSW HSC Modern History marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2024 NSW HSC Modern History exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting. The image attached before this text is the source the question refers to, in letter order; read it and judge how well the response uses it. Judge the response the way HSC Modern History markers do: a direct answer to the question, a sustained judgement where the directive verb asks for one, specific and accurate evidence (dates, names, cases, legislation, sources, historians) and the terms of the course. Do not reward length or narrative for its own sake.

Question 3 [15 marks]: To what extent does Source C accurately reflect the impact of Hitler’s dictatorship on German society between 1933 and 1939?

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 15):
13–15 marks: Makes a clear and sustained judgement about the extent to which Source C is an accurate reflection of the impact of Hitler’s dictatorship | Uses a wide range of relevant, detailed and accurate historical knowledge to support the judgement | Communicates historical ideas in a logical and well-structured response using a range of historical terms and concepts appropriately
10–12 marks: Makes a clear judgement about the extent to which Source C is an accurate reflection of the impact of Hitler’s dictatorship | Uses a range of relevant and accurate historical knowledge to support the judgement | Communicates historical ideas in a logical and structured response using a range of historical terms and concepts appropriately
7–9 marks: Makes a judgement about the extent to which Source C is an accurate reflection of the impact of Hitler’s dictatorship | Uses relevant and accurate historical knowledge in the response | Communicates historical ideas in a structured response using historical terms and concepts
4–6 marks: Provides a description about the accuracy of Source C and/or the impact of Hitler’s dictatorship | Provides a response using some relevant historical knowledge, terms and concepts
1–3 marks: Makes a general statement(s) in relation to Source C and/or the impact of Hitler’s dictatorship


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Possible theses:
1. Adolf Hitler’s rise to power in 1933 marked a turning point in German history, leading to profound transformation in various aspects of German society. Robert Ley encapsulates the essence of Hitler’s impact on German society during the years from 1933–1939 when he said ‘the broad large and great mass of our people has changed thoroughly. They have been transformed’ (Source C). While the lives of many were transformed others were not.
OR
2. Robert Ley’s quote in Source C is a substantially inaccurate interpretation of the impact of Hitler’s dictatorship on German society, while people’s lives were significantly changed, their beliefs were not transformed, they simply adhered to Nazi ideology for fear of what would happen if they did not. The Nazi regime altered the lives of German Jews, women and children to different extents.
• The ideology of the Nazi party permeated all elements of life
• Changes in the lives of workers eg lifting employment, increased working hours, lost protections of trade unions, forced to become part of the German Labour Front (DAF), subsidised holidays through Strength Through Joy Movement (KdF), etc
• Changes in the lives of women eg restricted professions, birth rates increased, role in creating the master race
• Changes in the lives of children (including education and youth organisations) eg schooling and curriculum changed, Hitler Youth was compulsory
• The impact of Nazi ideology on culture including books, music, art, architecture and film eg many artists were unable to stay in Germany
• Impact of the Nazi concept of race including Jews but also other racially inferior and superior people eg Jews were stripped of their citizenship and excluded from society, impact of Kristallnacht
• The impact of the Nazis on other minorities such as people with disabilities and homosexuals eg people with disabilities were sterilised
• The impact on religion (both the Nazi concept of religion and specific impact on Protestants and Catholics)
• People were constantly targeted by Nazi propaganda
• Nazi terror and repression including the SS, the Gestapo, concentration camps, the transformation of the legal system resulted in a society living in fear and/or targeted groups were significantly impacted
• Evidence that the ‘masses’ were not transformed include passive resistance, Germany was traditionally a conservative society so the lives of many were not transformed eg most women were housewives prior to the Nazis, resistance groups/individuals exist which show that not everyone was willing to conform.
